props.gloss_en: Rava's dilemma: if signs of tereifa arose in an etrog, what is its status -- is it unfit?
a lung poured out like a pitcher -- [the animal] is kosher
Rava: that is only where its bronchia are intact
Rava: but if its bronchia are not intact -- tereifa
the dilemma as the stam specifies it: an etrog in the like condition -- what is its status? is it unfit (the first horn), or perhaps there is no difference (the second horn)?
the first horn: perhaps it is there, where the air does not reach it, that it recovers; but here, where the air reaches it, it decays
a tafuach etrog is unfit
a saruach etrog is unfit
a pickled etrog is unfit
a boiled etrog is unfit
a Cushite etrog is unfit
a white etrog is unfit
a speckled etrog is unfit
a ball-shaped etrog is unfit
and some say: even the twin [etrog is unfit]
an unripe etrog -- R' Akiva deems it unfit
and the Sages deem it fit
if he grew it in a mould and made it like another form -- unfit
(entertained) is it not that tafuach is [decay] outside and saruach [decay] inside -- so an etrog decayed inside is unfit?
no: both are outside, and it is not redundant -- this where it swelled though it did not decay, that where it decayed though it did not swell
the mishnah: a Cushite etrog is unfit (the clause Abaye re-reads at 36a.7)
the second baraita: a Cushite [etrog] is fit
the second baraita: one resembling a Cushite is unfit
Abaye: when we learned the mishnah too, we learned [its unfit Cushite as] one resembling a Cushite
Rava: no difficulty -- this [ruling, unfit] is for us
and that [ruling, fit] is for them
Rabba: R' Akiva and R' Shimon said one and the same thing
R' Shimon exempts etrogim [from tithes] in their small state
Abaye (perhaps): R' Akiva says it only here, because we require hadar and there is none; but there [tithes] he holds like the Rabbis

Abaye (or else): R' Shimon says it only there, because it is written 'you shall surely tithe all the produce of your seed' -- [produce] as people bring it out for sowing; but here he holds like the Rabbis
Rava: they taught [unfit] only like another form; but in its own form -- fit
it is needed [for the case] where it is made plank-upon-plank -- [still its own form, so fit]
an etrog that mice pierced -- Rav: this is not hadar
R' Chanina would dip [and eat from] his etrog and fulfil [the mitzva] with it
the mishnah: pierced and missing any amount -- unfit (the clause Steinsaltz takes the קשיא מתניתין of 36b.3 to mean)
here [the mishnah] -- on the first festival day
there [R' Chanina's practice] -- on the second festival day
Rav could say to you: mice are different, for they are repulsive
some say: Rav said [of the mouse-pierced etrog]: this is hadar
